questions.stem: How much energy is needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 degrees C? (Specific latent heat of fusion of water = 334 000 J/kg)
questions.explanation: E = m x L = 0.5 x 334 000 = 167 000 J. Option B uses 1 kg instead of 0.5 kg. Option C uses 2 kg. The specific latent heat of fusion is the energy per kilogram needed to change a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point, with no temperature change.

questions.stem: What is the difference between specific latent heat of fusion and specific latent heat of vaporisation?

options.text: Fusion relates to melting/freezing; vaporisation relates to boiling/condensing
Fusion relates to boiling; vaporisation relates to melting
They are the same thing with different names
Fusion only applies to metals; vaporisation applies to water

questions.explanation: Specific latent heat of fusion (Lf) is the energy per kg to change between solid and liquid states. Specific latent heat of vaporisation (Lv) is the energy per kg to change between liquid and gas states. For water, Lv (2 260 000 J/kg) is much larger than Lf (334 000 J/kg) because more energy is needed to completely separate particles in boiling than to loosen them in melting.

questions.stem: A kettle supplies 452 000 J of energy to boil away 0.2 kg of water that is already at 100 degrees C. What is the specific latent heat of vaporisation?
questions.explanation: L = E / m = 452 000 / 0.2 = 2 260 000 J/kg. Option A multiplies instead of dividing. Option C uses mass = 1 kg. Option D divides by 2 instead of 0.2. This value (2.26 MJ/kg) is the accepted value for the specific latent heat of vaporisation of water.

questions.stem: A burn from steam at 100 degrees C is more severe than a burn from boiling water at 100 degrees C. Why?

options.text: Steam is at a higher temperature than boiling water
Steam releases latent heat energy as it condenses on the skin, in addition to the thermal energy from cooling
Steam particles are smaller and penetrate the skin more easily
Steam has less energy than water so burns feel more intense

questions.explanation: Both steam and boiling water are at 100 degrees C, so they start at the same temperature. However, when steam contacts skin, it first condenses, releasing a large amount of latent heat energy (2 260 000 J per kg). Then the condensed water cools further, releasing more energy. Boiling water only transfers the cooling energy. Steam actually has more energy than water at the same temperature, not less.

questions.stem: During an experiment, 3 kg of a substance at its melting point absorbs 600 000 J and completely melts. What is its specific latent heat of fusion?
questions.explanation: L = E / m = 600 000 / 3 = 200 000 J/kg. Option A multiplies E by m. Option C ignores the mass. Option D divides by 2 instead of 3. The specific latent heat is an energy-per-kilogram value, so you must divide the total energy by the mass of substance that changed state.
